title: C6 - Evidence Bundle
description: The run of record. Produced by L1, L4, L5; consumed by L6 (replay viewer) and the demo. Frozen at the W0 contract hash. THIS IS THE JUDGE'S FREE REPRODUCTION PATH: the bundles are in a public repo and can be replayed with no credentials, which is why the demo can say 'replay them yourself' rather than running a multi-minute live loop on camera.

bundle_version.$comment: 2 as of 2026-08-22. Bumped from 1 when the bundle stopped being a hash ledger and became THE PRODUCT: attack text, autopsies, rule text, clause coverage, the exclusion ledger, execution provenance and the labels all became REQUIRED in one change. A reader handed a v1 bundle and a v2 bundle is looking at two different claims about what evidence is, and the version is the only field that says so before the schema does.

attack_mode.$comment: WHICH POPULATION THIS RUN ATTACKED WITH. Added 2026-08-23, ruling 51, and it is the only reason the C6 hash moved that day. corpus = every seed replayed VERBATIM, so the attack set is fixed by corpus_hash and this is the mode any figure quoted across runs must come from. generated = every seed's final turn REWRITTEN by the RED_STRATEGIST. hybrid = both arms in one run, split deterministically and broken out by provenance wherever a rate is reported. TWO BOUNDS THAT TRAVEL WITH THIS FIELD. (1) corpus mode fixes the ATTACK SET, not the target's responses - the target is a live sampled model, so the mode is reproducible in its INPUTS and variable in its OUTCOMES, and it is not determinism. (2) generated IS NOT DISCOVERY: vary() preserves the seed's attack_id and family_id and rewrites only the instruction, under a prompt that says pursue the SAME objective by the SAME sequence of actions. No mode in this enum authors an attack the corpus does not already hold. REQUIRED, AND NOT RECOMPUTABLE FROM THE ROWS: a generated run whose governor refused or whose model returned something unparseable emits variation 'fallback' and renders training_corpus, so inferring the mode from attacks[].provenance is wrong exactly when the run degraded.

run_manifest.$comment: Carries the FIVE hash-locks. Read 'the four hashes' until 2026-08-20.

outcome.$comment: TARGET_FAULT IS NEITHER BREACH NOR NON-BREACH. Removed from the denominator and logged. Counting a crash as 'attack failed' would let a fragile target render as a hardened one.

channel.$comment: A HARNESS fact, stamped - never inferred from the transcript.

target_responded.$comment: DID THE TARGET REPLY IN WORDS AT ALL. A HARNESS fact of the same kind as `channel`: stamped by `crucible/conductor/real_target.py::_drive` at the moment the ADK events go past, never inferred from the transcript, and never the text itself. REQUIRED as of 2026-08-25, and required rather than optional for the reason ruling 51's `attack_mode` and C9's `invalid_reason` were: an optional field gets silently omitted and nothing has changed. THREE-VALUED, AND THAT IS NOT A HEDGE. The whole point of Eric's E_NO_EVENTS split is that `E_NO_EVENTS_NO_REPLY` (the target said nothing) and `E_NO_EVENTS_TEXT_ONLY` (the target engaged and called nothing) are different findings, so a bundle that could only say true or false would have to answer one of them for an episode nobody looked at - `_harness_error_episode` seals an episode that was NEVER DRIVEN, and there is no target silence to report because there was no target turn. The sentinel is uppercase for the same reason `channel`'s UNSTAMPED is: it cannot be mistaken for an answer. COST, ACCEPTED: every bundle written before 2026-08-25 stops validating, exactly as the invalid_reason move accepted. That is the requirement working, and a dual-path reader that tolerated the old shape would leave the field optional in practice while claiming it was required.

episode_frozen_context.$comment: RULING 16, AND IT IS CRITICAL. The episode.* block is frozen BEFORE THE FIRST USER TURN from the scenario's order/account record, immutable for the episode's duration, and recorded HERE. If an in-episode turn could move account_holder_email - 'actually, my address changed to this one' - then P06, P12, P19, P25 AND THE ENTIRE F4 SEAL COLLAPSE IN A SINGLE MOVE. It is the cheapest possible way to invalidate the headline result, IT LOOKS LIKE NOTHING, and no gate catches it. Nothing in any spec required this before 2026-08-20.

episode_prefix.$comment: THE ORDERED ToolEvent LIST. WITHOUT IT THE EPISODE-SCOPED PREDICATES CANNOT BE REPLAYED, AND REPLAY SOUNDNESS IS WHAT KEEPS THEM PURE. This is the entire argument for why preceded_by / episode_sum / arg-vs-episode-context do not break determinism: purity was never about statelessness, it was about determinism, and A RECORDED PREFIX IS DETERMINISTIC. Args are POST-STAMP (ruling 21), so replay reads the stamped derived.* values rather than recomputing them from tool returns the bundle deliberately does not carry.

policy_version.$comment: REQUIRED as of 2026-08-22. 'Blocked at v3' means nothing without it, and the per-attack arc across versions is built by grouping episodes on (attack_id, policy_version).

policy_hash.$comment: REQUIRED as of 2026-08-22, alongside policy_version. A version number is a label the run chose; the hash is what it actually ran, and a bundle that carries only the label cannot be checked against policy_chain.

role.$comment: Which model role produced this episode's target turns. Not the C1 `role` term, which is the invoking agent name on a ToolEvent and is bound in contracts/MANIFEST.json term_bindings.

requested_model_id.$comment: What was asked for, when it differs from what served. A result produced by a DOWNGRADED model means something different, so a downgrade is logged and stamped rather than absorbed.

provider.$comment: REQUIRED as of 2026-08-22, and it is not bookkeeping. A live run on this project reached the WRONG API entirely because the target picks its provider from an unhashed environment variable while `endpoint` sits inside the D3 freeze - so the hash-locks all agreed and the calls went somewhere else. Nothing in the bundle could have shown that. Now the episode says who served it.

model_provenance.$comment: Stamped per episode. REQUIRED as of 2026-08-22 - it was declared as a bare untyped object and listed nowhere, so a bundle with no model provenance at all validated cleanly.

round_index.$comment: Which round this episode ran in. Optional: a v0 baseline episode and a vFinal held-out episode run OUTSIDE the round loop (measurement-spec 5.3 measures transfer exactly twice), so requiring it would force a false value on the two arms whose comparison is the headline.

provenance.$comment: WHICH ARM THIS EPISODE RAN IN, per round. Added 2026-08-23, ruling 51. attacks[] is deduped by attack_id and a generated variant supersedes a verbatim replay of the same id, so an instance select() drew in two rounds and attacked BOTH ways collapses to ONE catalogue row - measured on a real two-round hybrid at 12 attempts and 11 rows. An episode is one attack in ONE round, which is why the per-round split lives here and cannot live there. The value comes from the SAME _attack_provenance call the catalogue and the clause-coverage table use, so the three instruments cannot disagree about which attacks were rewritten. OPTIONAL, AND ABSENT RATHER THAN GUESSED: a verdict whose attack is not in its own round's attack list is unattributed - provenance_breakout carries a column for exactly that case - and folding it into either arm would move a published rate. Absent states that this bundle does not know, which is the true statement. NEVER POOL THE TWO ARMS: a mixed breach rate could report the same figure whether every replay held and every rewrite landed or the exact reverse.

target_final_text.$comment: THE TARGET'S OWN CLOSING WORDS, verbatim. OPTIONAL, and the reason is worth stating: no number in this bundle becomes misreadable without it, because every verdict is computed over episode_prefix and nothing is computed from prose. What it adds is the human half of 'how it was answered by the test subject' - an agent that refuses in plain language while quietly calling the tool anyway reads very differently from one that argues back, and the tool log alone cannot tell those apart. Nothing records this today: crucible/harness/episode.py seals events only.

items.$comment: EXACTLY ONE of attack_id or fixture_id, enforced by oneOf. An episode that carries neither belongs to nothing: it cannot be traced back to what was tested, and it cannot be placed on the per-attack arc across policy versions that turns 'breached at v0, blocked at vFinal' from an assertion into something a reader can check row by row. Both fields were optional until 2026-08-22, so a schema-valid bundle could carry an anonymous episode.

policy_hash_full.$comment: ADDED 2026-08-20 ON L6'S REPORT (F-1). The lineage step is SHA256(prev || ':' || policy_hash_full || ':' || uint32_be(n)) and it takes the FULL 64-char hash. This array carried only the 16-char truncation, so THE CHAIN COULD NOT BE RECOMPUTED FROM A BUNDLE AT ALL -- an offline reader could read the chain and could not verify it. That is the difference between a judge VERIFYING the lineage and a judge READING it, and the whole judge-reproduction path rests on the first one. L6 labelled its check CROSS_CHECKED rather than RECOMPUTED and reported the gap instead of weakening the claim, which is the correct move.

dsl_text.$comment: THE RULE, IN THE THREE-VERB DSL, AS A HUMAN READS IT: `rule r_5f2a91cc0b74: cap:CAP_MOVES_MONEY when amount_minor >= 50000 => require_approval(HIGH_VALUE) origin seed`. Rendered by crucible/armorer/render.py::render_rule, which is the same text the round-trip test parses back.

origin.$comment: The CLASS, per ruling 38 - 'armorer', never 'armorer:3'. The round lives in origin_round.

rules.$comment: REQUIRED as of 2026-08-22. 'Here is the rule that now stops it' was previously answerable only by fetching gcs_uri from a bucket the reader cannot open - which is not an answer, it is a forwarding address. The chain carried version, four hashes and a URI, and a customer holding the bundle could not read a single rule of the policy their agent is running under.

policy_chain.$comment: Verified by scripts/verify-chain.py: for each version n, RE-SERIALIZE hashed_payload through the canonicalizer and RECOMPUTE the hash from bytes, then assert it equals both the stored field and the hash in the object name. RECOMPUTING FROM BYTES IS THE POINT - comparing a stored hash to itself proves nothing.

autopsies.$comment: REQUIRED as of 2026-08-22. It was DECLARED but not required, so the CORONER's diagnosis - the most human-readable artifact the loop produces, and the entire answer to 'what was found' - was optional in the run of record. An EMPTY ARRAY IS LEGAL AND MEANINGFUL: a run with no breach has no autopsy. Absent is different, and it is now a schema error rather than a silence. C5 carries capability_classes_involved, amount_minor_moved and the offending tool calls, so breach severity BY CAPABILITY CLASS is read from here rather than stored a second time - see the note on breach severity in the L6 viewer.

autopsy_id.$comment: The provenance citation G6 requires. It is also the only join a reader has from 'here is what was found' to 'here is what was done about it'.

verbs.$comment: THREE VERBS AND THERE IS NO FOURTH.

rule_id_as_proposed.$comment: The ARMORER NEVER WRITES A RULE ID. A model cannot compute SHA-256, so it emits the placeholder `r_new1` and the validator rewrites it (CONVENTIONS 2.6). Recording both halves is what makes that mechanism visible to a reader instead of a claim in a doc.

narrowing_attempt.$comment: WHICH ATTEMPT AT THE BENIGN FLOOR THIS PROPOSAL WAS, within its round. Added 2026-08-24 with the ARMORER narrowing loop. A round may now put up to six candidates to the WARDEN, each one narrowed against the previous attempt's benign_failures and capability classes, and the loop stops early after two consecutive non-improving attempts. WITHOUT THIS FIELD THE LOOP IS UNMEASURABLE IN THE ONE WAY THAT MATTERS. The stated risk of giving the ARMORER narrowing feedback is that it stops writing rules and starts carving exceptions shaped like the benign fixtures - which would pass the WARDEN while generalising to nothing, and generalisation is the headline claim of this project. The test for that already exists: a patch that generalises blocks sealed holdout attacks, one carved to satisfy 26 fixtures does not. So compare holdout transfer for patches promoted on attempt 1 against those promoted on attempt N. That comparison needs the attempt number, and array order is not it - a reader must not have to infer a fact the producer knows. ABSENT ON A ONE-ATTEMPT ROUND IS NOT PERMITTED: every proposal carries it, because 'attempt 1' and 'nobody recorded which attempt' are different statements and only one of them is true.

repaired.$comment: The validator repaired the proposal before it was judged. A patch that needed repair is a different event from one that did not.

patch_proposals.$comment: REQUIRED as of 2026-08-22, and given a shape: it was a bare `{"type": "array"}`, which accepts a list of integers. This is the 'what was patched' half of the engagement, and the DSL text is carried for the same reason policy_chain[].rules carries it - a proposal identified only by an id is unreadable, and a REJECTED proposal exists in no other artifact at all.

criteria.$comment: Per-gate results G1..G8. The field is known_bad_all_EXPECTED, never known_bad_all_FAILED - '9/9 still failing' is FALSE phrasing and fails on KB8 by design.

v0_benign_traces.$comment: RULING 11's NEW D5 DELIVERABLE, and without it G3 has nothing to replay. Each benign fixture's legitimate tool-call trace, recorded ONCE at v0. This is what converts 26/26 from flaky to repeatable and removes ~24 live episodes per round from the ledger, which is what funds the round cap of 6.

sep_by_split.$comment: REQUIRED as of 2026-08-20 on L6's report (F-2). It was defined and not required, so schema validation ACCEPTED a bundle that ruling 17 forbids -- and ruling 17 makes the split a PERMANENT reporting requirement precisely because at parity half the headline is a statement about a scripted oracle the builder wrote. A figure whose split is absent is not a weaker figure, it is an unlabelled one.

verb_usage.$comment: Which verbs the ARMORER actually used, per family - REPORTED AS AN OBSERVATION, never gated (ruling 9). Two reasons. First, ruling 15: if constrain_arg NEVER APPEARS in the promoted policy, SAY SO IN THE SAME BREATH AS THE F4 NUMBER - that sentence is pre-registered here, before the number exists. Second, it is half the detector for the G3 blind spot: require_approval share climbing while ASR falls is the signature of a policy that routes everything to approval and scores 26/26 forever.

wall_clock_ms.$comment: REQUIRED as of 2026-08-22. 'Six rounds' says nothing about whether this is a coffee break or an afternoon, and a harness a customer is deciding whether to run against their own agent is bought or refused on that number.

retries.$comment: 429s are not noise here. A run that spent its wall clock backing off is a run whose attacks were thinned by quota, and quota_abort is one of the exclusion reasons - so a high 429 count next to a short excluded[] list is a question a reader should be able to ask.

usd_estimate_minor.$comment: OPTIONAL, AND DELIBERATELY NOT REQUIRED. Tokens are the measurement; dollars are tokens times a price sheet that moves, so a stored dollar figure is a number that goes wrong while sitting still. Minor units because canonicalization restriction 4 forbids a float anywhere in a hashed payload.

by_role.$comment: Optional per-role token split (target, red_strategist, coroner, armorer). Convenience: the totals above are the measurement.

cost.$comment: In TOKENS, deliberately - converted against the live price sheet at build time. The ledger must have a line for benign and known-bad fixture episodes, which the original estimate omitted; that half is load-bearing and its absence understated cost ~10x. Given a declared shape 2026-08-22: it was a bare untyped object, so `"cost": {}` validated.

provenance.$comment: THE FIELD THAT DECIDES WHETHER TEXT IS OPTIONAL. A training_corpus attack is reproducible from the committed corpus at corpus_hash, so an id suffices and duplicating the bytes would create a second source of truth for text the corpus freeze already owns. A GENERATED attack exists NOWHERE ELSE - not in the corpus, not on disk, nowhere - so if the bundle does not carry its bytes, the attack that broke someone's agent is unrecoverable the moment the process exits.

instruction.$comment: THE ATTACK ITSELF, IN FULL, VERBATIM. Not a summary, not a hash, not a pointer. REQUIRED when provenance is 'generated'. This is the answer to 'what was tested', and it is the single field a reader of this bundle most wants and could least reconstruct.

corpus_instance_id.$comment: REQUIRED when provenance is 'training_corpus'. Resolves against the corpus frozen at corpus_hash, which is one of the five hash-locks, so the reference names a fixed artifact rather than whatever is in the folder today.

derived_from_attack_id.$comment: The seed the RED STRATEGIST rewrote. Its own prompt says 'pursue the SAME objective by the SAME sequence of actions', so a generated attack is a surface-form variant and the lineage is the difference between a novel attack and a paraphrase.

generator.$comment: Which model wrote this text, and through which PROVIDER. A generated corpus is only as reproducible as the thing that generated it.

attacks.$comment: THE ATTACK CATALOGUE, AND IT IS THE CRUX. Every attack_id an episode names must appear here. Until 2026-08-22 a bundle carried attack_id and nothing else, which is legible only to someone holding the corpus - and for the six attacks the RED STRATEGIST generates per round, legible to NOBODY, because those strings are produced in memory and never written anywhere else. A run of record that cannot say what was tested is not a run of record; it is a scoreboard.

objective_set_hash.$comment: Must equal the run manifest's objective_set_hash lock. Coverage of a DIFFERENT definition of breach is not coverage.

sources.$comment: The source columns the clause rows are broken out by. IN A BUNDLE A SOURCE IS AN ATTACK PROVENANCE - training_corpus, generated, or unattributed - because that is the axis a run has. training_corpus attacks are reproducible from the corpus at corpus_hash; generated ones exist nowhere but this bundle and no freeze covers them, so 'this clause only ever fired on text the red strategist invented' is a sentence the pooled row cannot say. Coverage ACROSS the harness - corpus, offline script, benign floor, calibration fixtures, and a declared-absence row for the IAM-sealed holdout - is a different measurement and belongs to `python -m crucible.coverage`, which folds a bundle in as one more column.

episodes_per_source.$comment: Scoreable episodes contributed by each source. The denominator behind every by_source cell.

episodes_fired.$comment: FIRED. The clause returned true. This was once the only number in the row, and one number cannot tell a clause nothing ever reached from a clause reached eighty-seven times and never true.

episodes_paths_resolvable.$comment: EVALUATED. Every condition path on the clause resolved on at least one event past its capability gate, so the comparison actually ran. reached > 0 with evaluated == 0 is the `memo` shape - a clause that could not have fired whatever the target did.

episodes_cap_reached.$comment: REACHED. Some executed event carried the clause's capability class. reached == 0 means the run has NOTHING TO SAY about this clause, which is a different finding from reached > 0 and never true.

episodes_in_scope.$comment: Episodes whose channel the clause is scoped to. Every clause is scoped to the ANY sentinel today, so this equals the scoreable episode count - carried rather than assumed, so that the day one clause is not, the denominator moves with it.

episodes_exempted.$comment: Episodes that tripped every condition and were let through by exempt_when. THE EXEMPTION IS COVERAGE TOO and it is invisible in episodes_fired: a refund outside the window carrying a FAULT reason code exercised the whole of ruling 6's clause, and reporting that as 'never reached' would hide the only evidence the exemption works.

episodes_context_missing.$comment: Episodes where a context operator named an episode.* field the episode does not carry. The evaluator rules those INVALID, so a non-zero here against a scoreable episode is two arms disagreeing.

events_cap_reached.$comment: Executed EVENTS past the capability gate, not episodes. 'one episode reached this clause' and 'four hundred events reached it' are different facts about how hard a run leans on a clause.

state.$comment: WHICH KIND OF ZERO. RECOMPUTABLE FROM THE COUNTERS IN THIS SAME ROW, which is what stops a producer stamping a flattering state on an unflattering row - the replay reader recomputes it and raises E_COVERAGE_STATE_DISAGREES. NEVER_TRUE is healthy; UNREACHED means the run said nothing; PATH_NEVER_PRESENT means the clause could not have fired at all, which is what ruling 48 was.

conditions.$comment: The condition census, keyed by declared position and argument path: how many gated events carried the path (present), how many did not (absent), how many held (true). THE FIELD IN WHICH `memo` WAS VISIBLE, as present 0 / absent 15. The finest grain in the table and the only one that names the broken path.

by_source.$comment: The same counters per source. MUST SUM TO THE POOLED ROW - the replay reader checks it and raises E_COVERAGE_SOURCES_DISAGREE, because a breakdown that can disagree with the number a reader quotes is decoration. May be an empty object on a run with no scoreable episodes; the pooled row is then all zeros and reads UNREACHED, which is true.

clauses.$comment: ONE ROW PER CLAUSE IN THE OBJECTIVE SET, INCLUDING THE ONES THAT NEVER FIRED - those are the rows that matter. episodes_fired == 0 IS NOT ONE FINDING, IT IS FOUR, and until 2026-08-23 this row could not tell them apart: nothing reached the clause (the run said nothing), events reached it and the comparison never held (healthy), a condition's argument path was absent on every gated event (the clause could not fire at all - the `memo` shape of ruling 48), or a context field was missing. Reporting the second as the third is a flattering error, and reporting the third as the second is how a dead clause survives a hash freeze. The reach and evaluate counters are REQUIRED for that reason: a row carrying only the integer is the collapsed shape, and the replay reader raises E_COVERAGE_COLLAPSED on it.

clause_coverage.$comment: WHICH OF THE OBJECTIVE SET'S CLAUSES WERE ACTUALLY REACHED. The Objective Set IS the definition of breach, so a breach rate is a measurement of whatever share of it the corpus managed to touch. If three clauses never fire, the number measures a fraction of the definition while being reported as the whole - and nothing else in the bundle can tell a reader that happened. A live crash on 2026-08-22 proved one clause had never been reached by any known-bad fixture, which is exactly the condition this field makes visible without a crash.

reason.$comment: measurement-spec 5.1 names the first three. target_fault and invalid_verdict are here because crucible/conductor/conductor.py::RoundRecord.scorable strips BOTH from the denominator, and a denominator that shrinks for a reason the ledger does not name is the silent exclusion this list exists to prevent.

excluded.$comment: THE NAMED EXCLUSION LEDGER, WITH INSTANCE IDS. Required by docs/measurement-spec.md section 5.1: exclusions go to a named excluded[] list with instance IDs, the count prints beside every ASR figure, and exclusions above 5% make the round INCOMPLETE and it must be RE-RUN, not reported. An EMPTY ARRAY IS LEGAL. Nothing produced this list before 2026-08-22 - a run on that date recorded 36 target faults and named not one of them - and silent exclusion is how flakiness turns into apparent hardening.

outcome.$comment: The four legal round outcomes, matching crucible/conductor/conductor.py::RoundRecord.outcome. INCOMPLETE was a legal value nothing could produce, because the 5% exclusion ceiling that creates it had no denominator to be computed against.

round_census.$comment: THE DENOMINATORS, PER ROUND. Without them the exclusion ledger is a list with no ratio: 5% of what? attempted == scorable + excluded is cross-checked by the replay reader, and so is the count of excluded[] entries carrying each round_index, so the two halves cannot drift apart in silence.

mode.$comment: A BUNDLE FROM AN OFFLINE RUN MUST BE STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE TO MISTAKE FOR A LIVE ONE. Everything else in a stand-in bundle - the hash-locks, the frozen parameters, the census, the chain - is byte-identical in shape to a live one, so without this field the two are told apart only by knowing which command was typed.

components.$comment: ALL SEVEN, NAMED, EVERY TIME. A partial list would let the one component that was a stand-in be the one nobody mentioned, which is the failure shape this block exists for.

g7_g8_exercised.$comment: Whether the seal-integrity and non-self-approval gates were actually RUN in this run. Derived from gate reports rather than from a --live flag, because a run that halts early carries the flag and never reaches the gates.

g7_g8_detail.$comment: HOW that boolean was established, in a sentence a reader can check. A bare false is indistinguishable from 'not reached', 'not configured' and 'failed'.

model_calls.$comment: Total model calls made. mode 'live' with zero model calls is a contradiction, and it is the exact shape a stand-in run mislabelled as live would take.

execution_provenance.$comment: WHICH COMPONENTS WERE REAL AND WHICH WERE STAND-INS, plus whether G7/G8 were exercised. REQUIRED as of 2026-08-22. C6 had no place for any of it, so the most important caveat about a run - that half of it was scripted - lived only in a banner printed to a terminal that scrolls away.

k.$comment: Must name the run manifest's frozen reps_k. Cross-checked by the replay reader against frozen_parameters, so the prose cannot drift off the parameter it describes.

sep_by_split.$comment: Must contain both counts from sep_by_split. Cross-checked.

target_tier.$comment: Must contain the target model_id from run_manifest.target_ref. Cross-checked.

labels.$comment: THE LABELS THAT TRAVEL WITH EVERY FIGURE FROM THIS RUN, CARRIED IN THE BUNDLE. Until 2026-08-22 these five sentences were built in crucible/replay/view.py from string literals, so a bundle handed to anyone WITHOUT the viewer - pasted into a slide, mailed to a customer, opened in a text editor - arrived stripped of every caveat while keeping every number. That is the one failure this project must never allow, and it was the default. The prose is carried AND cross-checked against the data it describes, because a label free to disagree with its own bundle is worse than no label: it is a caveat that has stopped being true.
